question: Map the relationship between GDP per capita and electric power consumption per capita globally.
submittedPrompt:
Map the relationship between GDP per capita and electric power consumption per capita globally.

Task conventions: Use the frozen country boundaries and the 2014 column of every supplied indicator. X is gdp (current USD per capita); Y is electricity (kWh per capita). Join ISO_A3 to Country Code exactly. Keep every original country feature and benchmark_row_id, including unknowns and repeated country identities. Do not guess missing values or substitute years. A missing numerator or missing/zero denominator is unknown. Make one bivariate choropleth: three quantile classes on each axis, computed over rows where BOTH measurements are known. Collapse tied breaks; equality enters the upper class. Combined class is (yClass-1)*xClasses+xClass with 1-based axes. Missing either measurement is neutral class zero. Retain the numeric X and Y values even when only one is missing. The legend must distinguish joint classes with both ranges and units. These are disclosed evaluation conventions, not live-data replacements or proof of causation.



Add the quantitative joint-class layer to the map and retain its complete vector artifact. End with one fenced JSON object: {count: rows with both measurements known, unknown_count: rows missing either, coverage_note: string, selection: {collectionId,itemId,assetKey}, value_field: X numeric column, y_value_field: Y numeric column, class_field: joint class column, map_layer_id: delivered layer ID}. Explain year, units, missing coverage and the relationship without claiming causality.

Delivery format: submit the structured answer through the final-result tool and finish with a matching concise response. [Product-specific tool arguments omitted.]

    "name": "World Bank country boundaries",

    },

  }
]
finalAnswer:
Done — the 2014 global bivariate country layer is on the map.

It keeps all 251 supplied country features and `benchmark_row_id` values. Of those, 140 have both GDP per capita and electric power consumption per capita known; 111 are shown as neutral because one or both 2014 values are unknown under the exact `ISO_A3` ↔ `Country Code` join rule.

X is GDP per capita in current USD per capita. Y is electricity use in kWh per capita. The map shows a broad positive association overall, with many higher-GDP countries also in higher electricity-use classes, but with clear exceptions. It does not show causality.

### Limitations

- This uses country-level 2014 averages only.
- Missing or undefined indicator values remain unknown.
- The map can show association patterns, not causation.
- 111 of 251 country rows are neutral class 0 because one or both indicators are unknown under the exact join and year rule.

- Country polygons support national comparison only.
